Shared workspaces now record a routable **entry origin** for the hosted web chrome: the share stack deliberately routes only `<label>.<domain>` origins on the relay (the bare workspace domain is unrouted, shielding it from Certificate-Transparency scanners), but the chrome iframed and health-probed the bare domain, so no workspace could ever open at `/web`. The connector reads the shell service's label from the workspace's `apps.toml` at share bring-up (claim and enable-sharing), records it on the share row (new `entry_label` column, migration 023, preserved when a later bring-up cannot supply one), accepts it from client-side share creates (`POST /shares`), and reports it from the claim response and share status. The chrome enters, probes, and iframes `<entry_label>.<workspace_domain>`, falling back to the bare domain when no label is recorded. Share status reads also accept the browser session cookie now (the chrome's health badges read them).

Fixed browser-session (cookie) authentication on every quota-checked resource endpoint the hosted chrome calls (`/hosts/claim`, `/hosts/lease`, `/keys/create`, `/keys/workspace-mint`, `/buckets`, the storage-cleanup grants): the entitlements resolution re-derived the caller from the `Authorization` header, so the hosted chrome's cookie-authenticated calls got a 401 "Invalid token". Callers now pass the user id their own authentication resolved (`/account/plan` was aligned to the same signature but stays Bearer-authenticated).

`POST /hosts/claim` now boots the adopted workspace: after the adopt rewrites the host record, the connector runs the template's shared start script (`minds_start_services_agent.sh`, the same one the VM-boot autostart units use) over SSH, so a web-created workspace comes up on its own instead of staying in the stopped state the bake left it in. A failed start releases the lease like every other post-lease failure, and runs before the share bring-up so it never leaves a share record for a dead workspace.

The set-a-master-password panel's copy now explains the Honest Software model ("we cannot see your data ... pick a master password that we don't know") with a learn-more link placeholder, replacing the generic key-protection sentence.

The web chrome now actually renders styled: its views wrote Tailwind classes as Mithril dotted selectors (`m("p.text-sm...")`), which Tailwind v4's source scanner cannot parse, so every layout utility was purged from the built CSS and the chrome rendered as bare HTML. All views now use explicit `class:` attributes (the same idiom as the desktop frontend).

The SuperTokens browser-session cookies are now set `SameSite=None; Secure; Partitioned` (CHIPS) instead of `SameSite=Lax`, so the accounts session is readable inside the hosted chrome's cross-site workspace iframe. Previously the broker's `/share/authorize` leg (which runs in that iframe) could not see the session, so the workspace owner was wrongly sent through the "Choose an account" interstitial instead of entering silently. CSRF protection is unchanged and does not rely on SameSite: every state-changing route already refuses a cross-site `Origin`, and session reads already run with the SDK's anti-CSRF check disabled (`anti_csrf="NONE"`, since our non-SDK frontends cannot supply the custom-header token the SDK would otherwise require when `SameSite=None`). The `Partitioned` attribute the SDK cannot emit is appended by a new response middleware. Existing signed-in sessions must sign in once to obtain the partitioned cookie.
